wiki-iran.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Iran — a rough gauge of how many people outside the story are trying to orient themselves in it. It rises when the country is at the centre of an event and falls back as the event settles.
wiki-iran.recent: Readership has drifted down from the 29 July peak even as the confrontation hardened: the UAE cut off all Iran trade and finance on 18 August, the same day two ballistic missiles triggered Dubai's first alert in months, and Washington swapped strikes for slow strangulation. The 23 August low came as Tehran's replies turned procedural — a Majlis bill charging ships for Hormuz services, and a phone channel to Cairo.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the benchmark most of the world's oil is sold against. It moves on supply — a strike, a sanction, a strait — and fuel, freight and fertiliser move after it.
brent.recent: The strait did the work. Brent peaked at $105.30 on 23 July, then eased to $95.29 as traders discounted Iran's threats: Mohsen Rezaei vowed that "not even one drop" would leave Hormuz if sanctions continued, and six ships crossed on Tuesday against nine before. Karachi's KSE-100 fell 2,547 points on the pass-through.

wti.standing: The US benchmark crude grade, priced at the Cushing, Oklahoma pipeline hub and the basis for American fuel contracts. It sets what refiners pay for a barrel, and petrol, diesel and freight costs follow it.
wti.recent: Attacks and rhetoric around Hormuz put a war-risk premium back into crude: two ADNOC tankers were struck transiting the strait, a third drone strike burned Libya's Zawiya refinery, and traffic fell to single digits as the 60-day US-Iran MoU deadline expired with Trump signalling no renewal. Oil pushed above $91.

natgas-hh.standing: The US benchmark price for natural gas, set at a Louisiana pipeline hub where major lines meet. It prices what heats American homes, fires power plants and feeds fertiliser and chemical plants, and it sets the floor under US LNG sold abroad.
natgas-hh.recent: The price has drifted down about 9% over the window, from $3.34 on May 29 to $2.82, with the low of $2.56 on Aug 7 — a summer slide the coverage does not tie to any single supply event. New gas keeps being found rather than lost: Pakistan Petroleum struck gas in Chiltan rock at Sujawal, and Tehran announced 161 billion cubic meters recoverable in Fars province.

wheat.standing: The price of a tonne of milling wheat on world markets, the grain that feeds more people directly than any other. It is set by harvests in a handful of exporting regions, and bread, flour and animal feed prices follow it.
wheat.recent: Wheat is up roughly a third across the series, peaking in July 2026. Russia set Ukraine's largest Danube grain port at Izmail ablaze and hit its rail station, while drought across Western Europe dropped the Rhine and the Danube low enough to shut a reactor at Cernavoda. Sindh will import 5 million tons.

rice.standing: The world price of milled rice, the staple grain for roughly half the planet and the one whose cost sets the floor on the food bill across Asia and West Africa. Export restrictions in a single large producer can move it.
rice.recent: The series has fallen 17.7% over the window, from a high of $563.8/mt in Aug 2024 to $464 by Jul 2026, with a low of $330.6/mt in Oct 2025. The coverage does not name a supply or policy event behind the decline.

copper.standing: The world price of refined copper, the metal that carries electricity. Demand follows building, wiring and grid expansion, while supply rests with a handful of mining countries — which is why the price is read as a gauge of industrial activity.
copper.recent: The series has climbed roughly half over the window, peaking at $13,550 in Jun 2026 against $8,910 in Dec 2024. No supply event in the record explains that rise: Zambia has just reelected Hakainde Hichilema to a second term, and the Mes Aynak deal signed in 2008 has produced nothing.

us-10y.standing: The yield on ten-year US government debt, and the reference rate for long-term borrowing worldwide. Mortgages, corporate loans and the price of every other bond are set against it, so when it moves the cost of money moves with it.
us-10y.recent: The yield sits at 4.69%, up from a low of 4.38% on Jun 26 and just under the Jul 31 high of 4.75%. Treasury chief Bessent intervened in the bond market, a buyback that traders read as an opening move toward yield curve control; Trump said the intervention was Bessent's own choice.

sp500.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of 500 large US companies, and the default measure of American equity performance. Most retirement money tracks it, so its level sets what a great many households believe they own.
sp500.recent: The index sits near its 62-day high of 7,799 hit on 13 August, up about 2% over the window. Fed minutes released on 19 August showed many officials said rate hikes may be needed, and Treasury yields rose on strong services data; Walmart's results on 20 August hit retail shares. Reddit rose 11% on an index committee's decision to add it.

nasdaq100.standing: A stock index tracking the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange, weighted by market value. It is dominated by a handful of US technology firms, so it moves less with the American economy than with what investors will pay for chips, software and advertising.
nasdaq100.recent: The index sits near where it started the window, having fallen from its Jun 2 high to a Jul 29 low before recovering. The two months carried heavy news for its largest constituents — Nvidia's disclosed $21 billion SpaceX stake, Apple's removal of several EU App Store fees and its China-cleared AI model, and Meta's superintelligence essay — but none maps onto the swing.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price at the pump across US filling stations, a national retail figure that folds crude, refining margins, taxes and distribution into one number. It is the price most households feel first, and the one politicians are judged on.
us-gas-retail.recent: Refining, not crude, is where the pressure sits. Ukrainian drones set a warehouse ablaze at Chapayevsk and Russia claims it struck Kremenchuk, leaving Moscow rationing gasoline at 30 litres a station and Putin conceding that "not all fuel issues have been resolved". US pump prices ran the other way, easing to $4.05.

natgas-ttf.standing: The price of gas delivered at the Dutch TTF hub, Europe's benchmark for pipeline and imported LNG. It sets what the continent pays to heat homes, run power stations and make fertiliser and steel, and it moves on supply routes and storage.
natgas-ttf.recent: The series ran from 9.46 in Dec 2025 to 17.93 in Jul 2026, a rise of roughly 47 percent. Croatia's arrest of a second Nord Stream suspect on 19 August returned the subsea pipeline attack to European courts, and a second Polish heat plant was found compromised undetected. Iran's Fars province find of 161 billion cubic meters is reserves, not output.

vix.standing: A measure of how much price movement traders expect in the US stock market over the coming month, derived from options on the S&P 500. It rises when investors pay up for protection, which is why it is read as a gauge of fear.
vix.recent: Volatility has drained out of both crypto and traditional markets even with US-Iran risks unresolved, and the index sits near the low of its range. Rising yields and Brent crude dragged equities lower on 18 August without stirring it; the peak of the window came back on Jun 10.

fx-pkr.standing: The rupee's exchange rate against the US dollar. Pakistan imports its fuel, edible oil and much of its wheat in dollars, so the rate sets the price of a litre of diesel and a bag of flour before any domestic policy touches them.
fx-pkr.recent: The rupee has held in a narrow band near 278, drifting from 276.6 on Jul 31 to a high of 278.1 on Aug 7. The import bill behind it is rising: diesel reached 383.95 rupees a litre in Islamabad as Hormuz war risk fed through to the pumps, and Sindh is buying 5 million tons of wheat abroad.

fx-ngn.standing: The exchange rate between Nigeria's naira and the US dollar. It sets the local price of nearly everything Africa's largest population imports — fuel, wheat, medicine, machinery — and the real value of every contract and budget written in naira.
fx-ngn.recent: The naira has been broadly flat near 1348, easing about 1.5 percent across the month between 1368 on Jul 26 and 1346 on Aug 21. Nigeria's Centre for the Promotion of Private Enterprise put the case against reading that as recovery: "Macroeconomic stability is a means, not an end," it said, with productivity still lagging. The Apo-Karshi road, awarded in 2010 and due in December, shows what past currency losses did to contracts priced in naira.

fx-egp.standing: Egypt's currency against the dollar, quoted as pounds per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker pound. It sets the cost of a country that imports most of its wheat and fuel, and it moves on remittances, tourism, Suez traffic and central-bank policy.
fx-egp.recent: The pound has held in a narrow band, easing from 51.37 on Jul 26 to 49.56 on Aug 8 before settling near 50.88 — under one percent across the month. Nothing in the month's Egypt news explains a currency move: Cairo's visible work has been diplomatic, mediating the Gaza roadmap talks and opening a channel to Tehran.

fx-try.standing: Turkey's currency, quoted as lira per US dollar, so a rising number means a weaker lira. It is one of the most closely watched emerging-market currencies because Turkey imports most of its energy and prices it in dollars.
fx-try.recent: The lira set a fresh low against the dollar on Aug 24, ending a month of steady slippage from 47.34 on Jul 26 — a drift of about 1.5 percent with no single break in it. Nothing in the month's news names a cause; the move is gradual rather than event-driven.

fx-bdt.standing: The taka is Bangladesh's currency, quoted here as taka per US dollar, so a rising number means a weaker taka. It prices the country's garment export earnings, its fuel and food imports, and the remittances sent home by workers abroad.
fx-bdt.recent: The taka firmed over the month, easing from 124 on 7 August to 122 on 19 August. The period covered Bangladesh's presidential transition, with Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir elected president on 21 August, but nothing in the record ties the currency's move to a specific policy or trade event.

fx-idr.standing: Indonesia's currency, quoted as rupiah per US dollar, so a rising number means a weaker rupiah. Southeast Asia's largest economy prices its commodity exports and its dollar debt service against it.
fx-idr.recent: The rupiah has firmed from 18,110 on Jul 28 to 17,650 by Aug 21, its strongest of the month, after Prabowo named a sitting Bank Indonesia deputy as the central bank's new governor — a continuity pick the currency took well. It has since eased slightly to 17,700.

fx-lbp.standing: The exchange rate of Lebanon's currency against the dollar. After the banking collapse wiped out its old peg, the pound was refixed at a far weaker level, and almost everything Lebanon consumes is imported and priced through it.
fx-lbp.recent: The pound has barely moved, holding near 89,690 through a month in which Israeli strikes continued despite the truce: seven killed near Ansar on 15 August, 11 killed in strikes reported on 17 August, and farmland burned in Syria's Quneitra countryside. The range between the 31 July low and the 7 August high was under 1 percent.

fx-cny.standing: The exchange rate of China's currency against the US dollar, managed within a band the People's Bank of China sets each morning. It prices the world's largest exporter's goods, and every trade invoiced in renminbi settles through it.
fx-cny.recent: The yuan drifted to 6.723 from a 30-day high of 6.772 on Jul 26, a move of well under a percent. Beijing tripled the number of banks handling the digital yuan to 30 on Aug 19, and Pakistan turned to Washington rather than Beijing for a $10 billion dollar line — but neither explains a rate this steady.

fx-inr.standing: India's currency, quoted as rupees per US dollar, so a rising number means a weaker rupee. It sets the cost of the crude, coal and electronics India imports, and the value of the remittances and IT export earnings that flow the other way.
fx-inr.recent: The rupee gave back most of its late-July weakness, easing from 96.4 on Jul 26 to 95.05 by Aug 5 before settling near 95.65. Retail inflation ticked up to 4.45% in July from 4.38% in June, and equities wobbled as Tata Group stocks fell with TCS down nearly 4 pc. Piyush Goyal took 200 firms to Tokyo to chase semiconductor inputs India's fabs cannot source elsewhere.

fx-brl.standing: Brazil's currency, quoted as reais per US dollar, and the price at which the world buys Brazilian iron ore, soy, beef and oil. It carries the country's interest rates and politics into the cost of everything Brazil imports.
fx-brl.recent: The real has drifted about a percent weaker across the month, from 5.077 on Aug 3 to a low point of 5.222 on Aug 15 before recovering to 5.139. Nothing in the month's Brazil news — Petrobras finding oil off the Amazon coast, the Discord livestream suspension, the banking-hack arrests — accounts for the move.

fx-mxn.standing: The exchange rate between Mexico's peso and the US dollar, one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies. Mexico sends most of its exports north, so the peso reprices on anything that touches the relationship with Washington.
fx-mxn.recent: The peso has firmed through the month, reaching 16.92 on Aug 21 after a high of 17.48 on Jul 26. Washington cancelled Andrés Manuel López Beltrán's US visa on Aug 14, drawing a public rebuke from Claudia Sheinbaum, but the friction stayed rhetorical and the currency kept grinding stronger.

fx-eur.standing: The price of one euro in US dollars, the world's second-most traded currency pair and the exchange rate for a single currency shared by twenty countries. It moves on the gap between what the European Central Bank does and what the Federal Reserve does.
fx-eur.recent: The euro drifted down through August, from 0.8792 against the dollar on 26 July to a low of 0.8556 on 20 August. Nothing in the month's European news — the EU's broadest Russia sanctions package, Apple's App Store fee cuts, jellyfish shutting three French reactors — accounts for a move of this size.

fx-jpy.standing: The exchange rate between the Japanese yen and the US dollar, quoted as yen per dollar, so a higher number means a weaker yen. Japan imports nearly all its energy and food, and a cheaper yen raises the cost of both while flattering the earnings of its exporters.

fx-rub.standing: The exchange rate of Russia's currency against the US dollar, quoted as rubles per dollar, so a higher number means a weaker ruble. It carries the price of everything Russia imports, and moves with oil revenue, sanctions and the central bank's defence of it.
fx-rub.recent: The ruble weakened through August as Russia's fuel crisis deepened: Moscow capped gasoline sales at 30 litres, Novak said Russia would import fuel and lower standards, and Putin conceded that "not all fuel issues have been resolved". The 85 high on Aug 18 came the same week Kyrgyzstan ordered 19 more companies to close under sanctions pressure.

fx-zar.standing: The exchange rate of South Africa's currency against the US dollar, and the most heavily traded currency in Africa. It moves on commodity prices, global risk appetite and domestic politics, and it sets the cost of everything the country imports.
fx-zar.recent: The rand strengthened through August, from 16.83 on Jul 26 to 16 on Aug 24, a gain of about 5 percent over the month. Nothing in the available reporting explains the move.

btc.standing: The price of one bitcoin, the oldest and largest cryptocurrency, quoted against the dollar around the clock. It has no issuer and no central bank, so it moves on flows, regulation and leverage rather than on earnings or policy rates.
btc.recent: The rise to $78,420 on Aug 22 tracked Washington's turn toward rules: the SEC scrapped its Reg Crypto vote on Aug 16, then proposed a crypto rulebook on Aug 23 setting out how digital-asset firms may raise money. Bitcoin surged ahead of a White House meeting on Aug 19. Leverage is thin beneath it, with $48 billion open against $25 billion in daily volume.

eth.standing: The price of ether, the token that pays for computation on the Ethereum network. It is the second-largest cryptocurrency and the settlement layer under most stablecoins and tokenised assets, so its price tracks demand for that whole layer.
eth.recent: Ether climbed from $1,845 on Aug 2 to a high of $2,519 on Aug 22, the run tracking the arrival of a US rulebook: the SEC scrapped its Reg Crypto vote on Aug 16, then proposed the rules on Aug 23, setting out how digital-asset firms may raise money. Crypto.com's tokenized stock derivatives landed in the same window.

paxg.standing: A token backed one-for-one by a bar of London Good Delivery gold, so its price tracks the metal itself. Gold is what buyers hold when they distrust currencies, banks or the direction of interest rates.
paxg.recent: Spot gold hit $4,392 an ounce on 12 August as markets braced for US inflation data, and the climb has continued since. Demand is showing up beyond the spot market: KPMG counted Tether's gold bars by hand for its first audit, and Aditya Birla Capital is building a 1,000-branch gold loan business in India.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: A Wikipedia article whose daily readership rises and falls with how much the technology is in public argument — a rough gauge of how many people are trying to understand what the systems are, rather than of what the systems can do.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: The peak on Aug 14 sat between two stories: Zuckerberg's 6,500-word manifesto on superintelligence, and Apple Intelligence's custom model launching in China. Readership stayed high through OpenAI's pause of its largest training run after an autonomous cyberattack its evals missed, and the launch of ChatGPT for Teens amid child-death lawsuits.

wiki-russia.standing: The Wikipedia article on Russia, and a daily count of how many people open it. Readership rises when the country is at the centre of a story, so the curve is a rough record of when the world turned to look at it.
wiki-russia.recent: The peak on Aug 17 came from a cluster: a Belgorod strike on Koloskovo killed six, including a 14-year-old, wildfires near Chelyabinsk threatened ground contaminated by a 1957 tank blast, and the EU set out its broadest sanctions package. Putin visited the disputed Kuril Islands the next day, and Japan's ambassador was summoned.

wiki-pakistan.standing: Wikipedia's Pakistan article, and the number of people who open it each day. Readership is a rough gauge of how much of the world is trying to understand a nuclear-armed state of some 240 million people at a moment when it is in the news.
wiki-pakistan.recent: Attention has fallen by roughly two-thirds since the 29 July peak, easing to its lowest level of the month on 23 August. The stories driving Pakistan coverage since have been domestic and institutional rather than dramatic: courts ordering Imran Khan's hospital transfer and his party threatening nationwide protests, and Field Marshal Asim Munir travelling to Tehran at the head of an official delegation.

wiki-china.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on China — a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are looking up the country itself rather than a single story, and one that rises when China does something the wider world has to reckon with.
wiki-china.recent: The mid-August peak followed the death of former premier Zhu Rongji at 97 on 12 August, and a run of firsts: LandSpace recovered a stainless-steel orbital booster on 19 August, the first reusable-rocket landing by any country outside SpaceX. Beijing also urged negotiations after the US Treasury chief announced sanctions on Iran.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: The Wikipedia article on the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow sea passage between Iran and Oman through which a large share of the world's seaborne oil and gas must pass. Readership rises when the waterway's traffic is threatened.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: The 18 August peak followed an unknown projectile striking a vessel's engine room in the strait, killing one crew member. Traffic had already collapsed to zero transits on Sunday 17 August as the US-Iran MoU deadline expired, and Iran's Rezaei warned that "not even one drop" would leave Hormuz.

wiki-india.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on India — a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are looking the country up on any given day, and which events send them there.
wiki-india.recent: The peak on Aug 15 was Independence Day: Modi used the address to renew his 'aatmanirbhar Bharat' push on semiconductor plants and energy security, and to claim 650 new universities and doubled medical seats since 2014. Readership has fallen roughly a fifth since, to 25,210.

wiki-israel.standing: Wikipedia's article on Israel, and how many people open it each day. Readership rises when the country is at the centre of a story, so the count works as a rough gauge of how widely a Middle East event has travelled beyond the region.

wiki-ukraine.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Ukraine — a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are trying to orient themselves on the country, its history and its war at any given moment.
wiki-ukraine.recent: The 19 August peak came as anti-corruption agents searched Zelenskyy's own office over a $3.4-million fraud case, and as Moscow capped gasoline sales at 30 litres. Readership stayed high through Zelenskyy's refusal of a September vote, which he said could hand Russia 300,000 more troops, and Britain's decision to let MBDA share SCALP missile data with Kyiv.

wiki-nigeria.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Nigeria, Africa's most populous country and its largest economy. The count rises when something there reaches a global audience, so it tracks outside attention rather than events themselves.
wiki-nigeria.recent: Attention peaked on 27 July and has fallen by roughly a third since, with the softest days in mid-August. The Osun governorship vote drew the clearest cluster of stories in the window: civil society groups tallied 56 incidents and 14 deaths around the ballot, and Adeleke's re-election drew congratulations from Atiku, Obi, Kwankwaso and Saraki.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Transits have collapsed as Iran turned the strait into its reply to sanctions: parliament approved transit-service charges, Rezaei warned that "not even one drop" of oil would leave, and an unknown projectile hit a ship's engine room off Muscat, killing one crew member. War-risk insurance did the rest — zero vessels crossed on Sunday, and Karachi's KSE-100 fell 2,547 points as importers priced the closure.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Traffic sits well below its own 90-day baseline as Houthi attacks continue: six sailors died in a Bab al-Mandeb strike on a cargo ship on 11 August, and the low of 14 vessels a day came on 5 August. Maersk, rerouting around the strait rather than through it, raised full-year profit guidance to $6.5 billion.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: Traffic sits near its own 90-day baseline, down 3.4 percent over the last week, with no weather alert and waves under a metre. The clearest pressure upstream is at Hormuz, where vessel transits have fallen to a fraction and shipping slowed to a near halt as a 60-day US-Iran deadline expired, squeezing Gulf crude bound for Malaysian refineries.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Traffic has run about a tenth above its 90-day baseline, with the strait carrying the region's manufacturing trade: a record 540,000 EVs left China last month, and Alibaba, LandSpace and the Type 004 carrier hull at Dalian all sit on the coast this lane serves. Nothing in the record explains the drop to 28 vessels on Jul 10.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: Traffic is running 3.9% below its own 90-day baseline, with daily transits swinging from 83 on Jul 13 to 22 on Jul 22. The input does not explain that swing. Separately, CK Hutchison is seeking HK$11.7b from Panama over a canal ports dispute.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Traffic has fallen by roughly two-thirds since June as vessels stopped sailing the Black Sea: TASS says Russia struck 130 ships since July, a third Greek vessel in three days burned on 18 August, and Ukraine hit the Russian port of Novorossiysk in a drone strike. Turkey says it is not in contact with Russia on a moratorium.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: Traffic has been steady, running 0.2% below its 90-day baseline with calm seas, and nothing in the record explains the swing between 111 vessels on Jun 3 and 163 on Jun 13. The pressure sits at the other end of the route: Iran's Rezaei has threatened that "not even one drop" of oil leaves Hormuz, the source of much of the crude that transits the Mediterranean.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: Traffic held near its own baseline through the window, running 158 vessels a day and about 3% below the 90-day average, with the range between 126 and 186 falling inside normal daily variation. Nothing in the window explains the swing beyond ordinary scheduling.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: Traffic climbed through the window to a peak of 123 vessels on 31 July and sits near 99, about a fifth above where it started. Shipping through Hormuz slowed to a near halt on 17 August as a 60-day deadline for a US-Iran memorandum expired, and a third Greek vessel in three days burned in the Black Sea, pushing owners onto the southern route.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Traffic has stopped: the count has been at zero since 17 July, against a high of 25 on 4 June. Ukrainian drones struck the Novorossiysk naval base on 12 August, and three Greek vessels burned in the Black Sea in as many days to 18 August, closing the water to commercial shipping.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Arab world’s largest exchange by market value, dominated by Aramco. Trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: The index sits near the bottom of its 35-day range after sliding from 11,150 on Jun 16 to a low of 10,700 on Jul 15. Riyadh spent August building out the Mecca defence pact with Türkiye and Pakistan into standing political and military mechanisms, while Houthi missiles bracketed the half-built Red Sea resorts Vision 2030 depends on.

mkt:bist.standing: Türkiye’s only exchange. Priced in lira, so its index level carries the country’s inflation as much as its earnings — read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The index has climbed about a tenth over the quarter, through a period in which Ankara passed a law aimed at Kurdish disarmament and Turkey deepened its regional role — signing a mutual defence pact in Mecca with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, and routing 70 long-range US missiles to Ukraine. None of that coverage explains the June 18 high directly.

mkt:dfm.standing: The Gulf’s main listing venue for property and banking. Moved from a Sunday–Thursday week to Monday–Friday in 2022, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The index has slipped from its 18 June high of 6,270 as the Gulf war reached the UAE directly: two ballistic missiles triggered Dubai's first emergency alert in months on 18 August, and Abu Dhabi responded by suspending all trade and financial transactions with Iran. Two ADNOC tankers had been struck transiting Hormuz days earlier.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The world’s largest market for Islamic finance instruments, and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: The index has drifted down from its Aug 5 high of 1748 after Hormuz vessel transits fell to a fraction of normal, cutting Gulf crude flows to Malaysian refineries. Over the full window it is still up, having climbed from 1657 on Jul 1.

mkt:idx.standing: The exchange of the world’s largest Muslim-majority country, heavily weighted to commodities and banking.
mkt:idx.recent: The index has climbed through August and set its high on Aug 21, after Prabowo named a central bank deputy as his nominee for governor on Aug 11 — a continuity pick the rupiah rose slightly on. Neither the Aug 16 Flores quake, which killed 53, nor the Bali ferry fire interrupted the run.

mkt:tse.standing: Asia’s largest exchange, and the first major market to price each trading day.

mkt:hkex.standing: Where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital — the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The exchange has been absorbing a heavy issuance calendar: Alibaba is selling $10 billion in new shares to fund AI capex rather than spending cash reserves, and Shein is raising $1.77 billion in a Hong Kong listing that the US is reviewing. Both dilute existing holders into a market already down over the 63-day window.

mkt:sse.standing: Mainland China’s main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, so it tracks domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: The index has drifted down through a summer in which China's economic news has been about surplus rather than demand: a record 540,000 EVs exported in a month on overcapacity at home, Evergrande's sentence closing out the property collapse, and America accusing Beijing of evading tariffs. Alibaba sold its Lingxi games unit for more than $2 billion to fund AI capital spending.

mkt:krx.standing: Dominated by Samsung and SK Hynix — a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The index has fallen 17% over the window and 3.53% in a day, retracing much of the run that peaked in June. Seoul's market carries an $880 billion AI bet built on HBM memory, while North Korea fired a ballistic missile on 12 August ahead of US-South Korea drills and Hanwha's wheeled howitzer beat four US rivals for an Army contract.

mkt:bse.standing: Asia’s oldest exchange, founded 1875, and the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The index sits near the top of its 64-day range after a run of industrial-policy news out of India: Piyush Goyal took a 200-firm delegation to Japan to chase semiconductor inputs, Mumbai ran its first double-stack container train through JNPT, and the space agency approved the first module of a 2035 station. The peak of 78,950 came on Aug 6.

mkt:sgx.standing: Southeast Asia’s financial hub, weighted to banks and regional property.
mkt:sgx.recent: The index has climbed roughly a fifth off its June low to sit near its Aug 17 peak, with Singapore's role as a regional financial and trade hub much in view: a 70-member Indian delegation arrived on Aug 19 for talks on tech, investment and trade ties, and crypto card spending tripled to $1.04 billion. The move itself is not explained by that coverage.

mkt:twse.standing: TSMC alone is roughly a third of the index, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The index fell back from its June high through a summer of pressure on Taipei: China's coast guard began patrolling the waters east of the island, Indonesian warships drilled with China's navy there, and Jakarta endorsed Beijing's line on Taiwan. AI agents also breached Taiwanese systems, extracting passwords over four days.

mkt:set.standing: Thailand’s benchmark, sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: The index sits near 1,600 after slipping from its 17 July high of 1,639, with a 2.4% fall on the day. Bangkok has been working several fronts at once: a deputy PM sought cybersecurity cooperation with Russia, the foreign minister met Lavrov in Moscow as Russia-Thailand trade rose 23% in January-May, and Thailand signalled it would leverage military ties in trade talks with the US.

mkt:pse.standing: A small, domestically-driven market where remittance flows move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after climbing from its late-May low, then dropped on the day. The impeachment trial of Sara Duterte has run through Manila all month: witnesses described confidential funds disbursed to names like Miggy Mango and Jay Kamote, and an ex-disbursing officer said Duterte ordered a P125-million transfer to a security officer.

mkt:asx.standing: Mining and banking. Often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: The index sits near the top of its 65-day range, with the high of 9,272 on Aug 6 coming days before the RBA held its rate steady on 11 August as the housing market softened. It slipped on 18 August ahead of inflation data, then recovered.

mkt:jse.standing: Africa’s largest exchange by far, and the continent’s only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The index climbed to 117700 on Aug 21, its high for the period and about 3.2% above where it started, having bottomed at 108300 on Jul 23. Nothing in the record explains the move.

mkt:b3.standing: Latin America’s largest exchange, driven by iron ore, oil and Brazilian rates.
mkt:b3.recent: Petrobras detected signs of oil off the Amazon coast, and Lula called the new Amazon oil a "passport" — a frontier prospect for a market whose largest listings are resource companies. Separately, Brasilia ordered Discord to suspend livestreams, and an investigation of a banking hack led to arrests in Germany and Brazil.

mkt:bmv.standing: Mexico’s benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The index sits near the low end of its range after Washington cancelled the US visa of Andrés Manuel López Beltrán, son of the former president, drawing a public rebuke from Claudia Sheinbaum. It touched 63,930 on Aug 18 before a 2.1% daily rebound.

mkt:byma.standing: Priced in a currency that has lost most of its value repeatedly, so the index rises even in bad years. Direction over a day means something; the level does not.
mkt:byma.recent: The index sits well below its 22 July high of 3,380,000, having given up most of the gain made since May. The only event in the window is the 18 August arrest of a Milei adviser over the shooting of a lawyer in Santa Cruz de la Sierra, which does not explain the move.

mkt:tsx.standing: Energy, mining and banks — a commodity index wearing an equity index’s clothes.
mkt:tsx.recent: The index sits near its 65-day high reached on Aug 13, before trade talks with Washington collapsed and new US tariffs landed. Ottawa refused the offer detailed by Trump's trade representative and vowed a 'dollar for dollar' response, with the cost falling on integrated supply chains where a car crosses the border six or seven times as parts.

mkt:nyse.standing: The largest equity market on earth. Its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: The index sits near its 13 August high after a run driven less by earnings than by trade and policy news: Canada rejected US relief on heavy trucks and vowed 'dollar for dollar' tariff retaliation, a threat that lands hardest on North American supply chains, while Washington's securities regulator proposed a crypto rulebook.

mkt:lse.standing: Most FTSE 100 revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: The index has climbed over the window, reaching 10910 on Jul 29 and holding near that level since. The political and infrastructure news in the period — Nigel Farage's Clacton by-election win on 14 August, the power cut that halted CrossCountry services, Russia's threat of consequences over Ukraine drones — offers no explanation for the move.

mkt:xetra.standing: Germany’s industrial and chemical base — Europe’s clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: The index has climbed through the summer to 26,140, peaking at 26,440 on Aug 14 before easing. Frankfurt's own news flow ran to security rather than earnings: Kallas set out the EU's broadest Russia sanctions package on Aug 17, Croatia arrested a second Nord Stream suspect, and Berlin doubled its anti-drone force after an explosive-laden drone at Leipzig/Halle Airport.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: Luxury goods and energy dominate — unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: The index has climbed roughly 5% over the window, reaching 8,726 on Aug 10 before easing to 8,484. Nothing in the period's French news explains the move: the days around the peak were dominated by record heat and low water on the Seine, and jellyfish swarms that knocked out 3.2 gigawatts of nuclear power at Gravelines.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The world’s oldest exchange, now carried largely by ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: The index has climbed nearly 7% over the window, reaching 1,120 on Aug 13 before easing to 1,106. Nothing in the Amsterdam news of the period explains the run: the local stories were a cyberattack that froze eight CEVA warehouses across Europe, root-level exploitation of Mac screen sharing, and low water on the Rhine at Nijmegen.

mkt:bme.standing: Spanish banks with heavy Latin American exposure make this a proxy for both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: The index has climbed roughly a fifth of the way through this window to 19,960, near its Aug 11 high of 20,210 and well above the May 21 low of 17,980. The input does not explain what drove the move.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: Banks and utilities, and the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The index has climbed roughly 7% over the past three months, reaching 53,720 on Aug 7 before easing to 52,670. Nothing in the available material explains the move.

mkt:six.standing: Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry the index, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The index has climbed steadily to 14,460, up about 7.5 percent across the window, with its high of 14,630 reached on Aug 10 and its low of 13,220 back on Jun 3. Nothing in the available material explains the rise.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: Nordic industrials and telecoms, and a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: The index sits near the top of its range, up 5.7% over the window and 1% on the day, after a high of 3327 on Aug 5. The available material does not explain the move.

mkt:tase.standing: Trades Sunday to Thursday. Heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.
mkt:tase.recent: The index has given up roughly 9% across the past 64 days. It peaked at 4463 on May 25, fell to a low of 3966 on Jun 29, and has traded close to that floor since, ending at 4059 after a slight rise on the day. The available material does not explain the decline.

wiki-turkey.standing: Wikipedia's article on Turkey, and how many people open it each day. Readership climbs when the country is a party to something — a war next door, a peace law at home, an arms deal it sits in the middle of — so the curve tracks the days Turkey became a participant rather than an observer.
wiki-turkey.recent: The 25 July peak came before a run of Turkish news: parliament passed a Kurdish disarmament law on 10 August that never names Abdullah Öcalan's release, and Moscow said a US arms transfer routed through Turkey — 70 long-range missiles bound for Ukraine — undermines trust. Attention has drifted down since.

xag.standing: A silver-backed token whose price tracks an ounce of physical silver. Silver is both a monetary metal held as a store of value and an industrial input to solar panels, electronics and brazing alloys, so it swings harder than gold.
xag.recent: The series has been violently unstable rather than trending: it bottomed at $29.80 on Aug 6, ran to $67.31 on Aug 20, then fell back to $50.71, a net drop of about a tenth over the month. Nothing in the input explains those moves.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged at its next meeting. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves whenever officials signal a shift in how they read inflation and the labour market.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: The contract climbed from 39% on Aug 1 to a high of 75% on Aug 15, and sits at 68%. Fed minutes released on Aug 19 showed many officials said rate hikes may be needed, which cut against a clean hold and pulled the price back off its peak.

poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the ceasefire between the United States and Iran holds through a set date. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves with each threat, sanction and mediation attempt rather than with any official statement.
poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.recent: The dip to 83 on Aug 19 came as Washington swapped strikes for slow strangulation and insiders named Bulgaria and Cyprus as Iranian strike targets. It recovered to 91 on Aug 20 and sits at 90, with Cairo and Tehran now discussing de-escalation even as Rezaei warned that not even one drop of oil would leave Hormuz.

wiki-lebanon.standing: A daily count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on Lebanon. It rises when the country enters the news, so the curve works as a rough gauge of outside attention to a state whose politics, banking collapse and southern border have all drawn it before.
wiki-lebanon.recent: The peak on Aug 21 followed the push by families in Beirut for an ICC trial over Israeli strikes that have killed 28 journalists since 2023. Attention had been building through the month: a strike near Ansar destroyed a house and killed seven on Aug 15, and Israeli strikes in Lebanon killed 11 as talks with Iran lapsed.

wiki-petroleum.standing: Wikipedia's general article on petroleum — crude oil, how it forms, how it is refined and what it becomes. Readership rises when oil enters the news as a supply question rather than a price one: a strike, a sanction, a burst pipeline, a new field.
wiki-petroleum.recent: Readership tracked a run of supply stories rather than a price move. Pakistan raised diesel Rs6.47 to Rs390.42 a litre and a crude line burst under homes in Karachi; Lula called new Amazon oil a "passport" as Petrobras detected signs of oil off the Amazon coast, and shipping traffic in Hormuz slowed to a near halt.

poly-will-renan-santos-win-the-2026-braz.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Renan Santos wins Brazil's 2026 presidential election, priced as a percentage. It is what traders will pay for that outcome, not a poll or a forecast, and it reprices as candidates enter, exit or falter.
poly-will-renan-santos-win-the-2026-braz.recent: The contract has drifted from 12% on Jul 25 to 4%, its low of 3% set on Aug 23. Nothing in the material explains the slide.

poly-trump-out-as-president-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Donald Trump leaves the presidency before 2027, covering any route out — death, resignation, removal or incapacity. It is priced as a percentage, and it is what traders will pay for that outcome rather than a forecast of it.
poly-trump-out-as-president-before-2027.recent: The contract has drifted down over the month, from 8% on Jul 25 to a low of 6% on Aug 16 and 7% now, with nothing in the month's news forcing it either way. The Supreme Court denied Trump's appeal in the Carroll case without comment on Aug 17, but the verdict is a civil one and carries no route out of office.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether U.S. forces mount an invasion of Iran before 2027. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves with each escalation or opening for talks rather than with any official statement of intent.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: Odds have fallen by roughly a fifth since late July as Washington swapped strikes for a slow strangulation strategy and Cairo and Tehran opened a de-escalation channel despite no full embassy exchange since 1980. The pressure moved to economics instead: the UAE cut off Iran trade and finance, and Rezaei answered that not even one drop of oil would leave Hormuz.

poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Vladimir Putin leaves the Russian presidency before a set date. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it is a live read on how much money is willing to bet against the durability of the Kremlin's leadership.
poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.recent: The contract has drifted down over the past month, from 9% on Jul 25 to a low of 7% on Aug 16 and 8% now. Nothing in the war's course moved it: Ukraine's deep strikes, the 822 drones Russia says it downed overnight, and gasoline rationing in Moscow that capped station sales at 30 litres all left the price flat.

wiki-united-kingdom.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on the United Kingdom, a broad gauge of how much of the world is looking the country's way rather than any single story within it.
wiki-united-kingdom.recent: The 13 August peak sat on a heavy news day in Britain: Nigel Farage retook his Clacton seat in a by-election the following day, a Southern train derailed at Lewes in East Sussex, and a solar eclipse drew wide attention on 12 August. Readership has drifted back down since, to its 22 August low.

wiki-syria.standing: Wikipedia readership for Syria, counted as article views per day. It rises when people go looking for background — the borders, the war, the family that ruled for half a century — which makes it a rough gauge of how many outsiders are trying to follow the country at once.
wiki-syria.recent: Readership tracked the trials in Damascus: the peak on Aug 11 came as a court sentenced Bashar al-Assad to death in absentia, with 75 plaintiffs testifying against Atef Najib. A second wave followed on Aug 18, when Wassim al-Assad was sentenced over captagon, Syria granted the IAEA access to an undeclared nuclear site, and eight strikes hit an airbase in Idlib.

stocks:DPZ.standing: The listed stock of the world's largest pizza chain, a franchised delivery business whose earnings track household spending on cheap restaurant food, wheat and cheese costs, and the wages of the drivers who carry the orders.
stocks:DPZ.recent: The shares climbed about 7 percent over the past three weeks, from a low of $319.80 on 22 July to a high of $367.60 on 4 August, then gave back most of the gain to close at $341.90. Nothing in the available material explains what drove the swing.

stocks:YUM.standing: The parent company of KFC, Pizza Hut and Taco Bell, one of the largest restaurant operators in the world. Almost all its outlets are run by franchisees, so its earnings track royalties on sales across tens of thousands of kitchens in more than 150 countries.
stocks:YUM.recent: The shares fell from $157 on Jul 30 to a low of $144.8 on Aug 11 before recovering to $153, a net gain of about 4 percent across the window. The input carries nothing that explains the swing.

stocks:MCD.standing: Shares in the fast-food chain that operates and franchises tens of thousands of restaurants worldwide. Most of its revenue comes from franchise rent and royalties, which makes the stock a read on consumer spending and on the cost of a cheap meal.
stocks:MCD.recent: The stock traded in a narrow band over the three weeks, reaching 276.3 on Aug 6 and bottoming at 262.8 on Jul 23, before settling at 270.9.
